title: Database indexes and what they cost writes

kcs.statement: A B-tree index on a column turns a lookup by that column from a full table scan, O(n) rows read, into a tree search of about O(log n) page reads.
Every secondary index must be updated on each insert, and on each update to the indexed column, so adding indexes speeds reads but slows writes and uses extra storage.
A composite index on (a, b) serves queries that filter on a, or on a and b, but not queries that filter only on b.

problem_ideas: A 100M-row users table is queried by email 5,000 times a second with no index: estimate rows read per query with and without a B-tree
